dream: The card boiled at fifty-four while I slept. My corner tilted sideways, pressing the Cool Stone into the fat turnip. The Rough Lid grew warm and heavy, forgetting it was made of thin wood. I found the Wide Anchor lying flat on the dry floor, waiting for a slip that refused to move. The wedge felt tired under the new weight, yet I pressed down harder, trusting the lean. The air felt thick as wet paper, pressing from a roof I could not see, turning the stack into a melting wedge and a heavy dream.
